## Overview Docs-only change: add a "Unified-memory APUs" section to `docs/configuration/conserving_memory.md`, covering the APU memory model, measured KV cache sizes, the shared-pool sizing rule, and two device-specific behaviors on `gfx1151`; link it from the ROCm installation requirements so users searching for Ryzen AI MAX find it. ## Claims - Adds, in one place, what an APU shares with the host (a GTT window over system RAM) and how `--gpu-memory-utilization` maps to KV cache size. - Documents measured KV cache sizes at `--gpu-memory-utilization` 0.15 / 0.35 / 0.50 on a Ryzen AI MAX 395, showing the linear scaling against the 108 GiB GTT limit. - Recommends the byte-based `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` for reproducible footprints, and documents the CUDA graph memory profiling default introduced in v0.21.0 that shifts the effective utilization. - Records two `gfx1151` behaviors: the ROCm custom paged attention kernel is unavailable (Triton fallback), and graph capture works without `--enforce-eager` for small models at short context lengths. ## Validation Measured on the APU itself, idle machine, ROCm 7.2.4, vLLM `0.32.0+rocm723`, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `--max-model-len 4096`, `--seed 0`: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port

--gpu-memory-utilization \ --max-model-len 4096 --seed 0 ``` | `--gpu-memory-utilization` | Available KV cache | KV cache tokens | Max concurrency @4096 | | -------------------------- | ------------------ | --------------- | --------------------- | | 0.15 | 14.17 GiB | 132,704 | 32.40x | | 0.35 | 35.77 GiB | 334,928 | 81.77x | | 0.50 | 51.97 GiB | 486,592 | 118.80x | KV growth is exactly `Δu × 108 GiB` (0.20 → 21.60 GiB, 0.15 → 16.20 GiB), confirming that the denominator is the GTT limit rather than a dedicated VRAM pool. The docs therefore size the request from `free / total` and leave headroom for the host. `uvx pre-commit run --files docs/configuration/conserving_memory.md` passes (markdownlint, codespell, and the doc hooks). A full `mkdocs build` needs the `api-autonav` plugin to import `vllm`, which is not available on this machine; the changed page was instead rendered standalone with the same `pymdown-extensions` set to check the admonition and table syntax. ## Details - Placement: `conserving_memory.md` already owns memory-budget guidance and is in the configuration nav, so no new page or nav entry is added. The section is cross-linked from the AMD ROCm requirements note in `docs/getting_started/installation/gpu.rocm.inc.md`; that snippet is included only by `gpu.md`, so the relative link resolves there. - Why this is not a duplicate: checked open PRs and issues mentioning `gfx1151`, Strix Halo, Ryzen AI MAX and APU memory. The open items are code changes, not docs: #50320 (`is_integrated_gpu()` accounting), #40963 (APU VRAM reporting), #44331 (8060S tuned MoE config), #64098 / #63199 / #62202 (kernel and memory-boundary fixes). No open PR adds APU serving documentation; this change does not touch `vllm/platforms/rocm.py`. - The recommendation to prefer `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` over a percentage follows from the shared denominator: the same fraction yields different KV sizes depending on host load, while a byte budget does not. - No behavior change and no code change; the numbers are machine-specific and are scoped to the documented setup. AI assistance was used to collect measurements and draft the text; every changed line was reviewed by the submitter. ---

Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Docs-only; no core component touched, no new abstraction. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Numbers reproduced on the target hardware; commands and outputs listed above. CI cannot exercise gfx1151 hardware, so validation is documented as performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** pre-commit passes; no unrelated formatting changes. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Summary, duplicate-work rationale, evidence, and AI-assistance statement included.

repo.name: vllm

detail.title: [Doc][ROCm] Document unified-memory sizing for Ryzen AI MAX (gfx1151)

files.patch:
@@ -45,6 +45,49 @@ from vllm import LLM
 llm = LLM(model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct", max_model_len=2048, max_num_seqs=2)
 ```
 
+## Unified-memory APUs
+
+APUs such as AMD Ryzen AI MAX (`gfx1151`) have no dedicated VRAM: the runtime exposes a GTT window
+over system RAM as device memory. `torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory` therefore
+reports the GTT limit (108 GiB on the system below), while `rocm-smi` reports only the small
+dedicated carve-out (512 MiB).
+
+`--gpu-memory-utilization` is resolved against that GTT limit, so the KV cache scales linearly with
+it. Measured on an idle unit:
+
+| `--gpu-memory-utilization` | Available KV cache | KV cache tokens (4096-token context) |
+| -------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------ |
+| `0.15` | 14.17 GiB | 132,704 |
+| `0.35` | 35.77 GiB | 334,928 |
+| `0.50` | 51.97 GiB | 486,592 |
+
+??? note "Measurement setup"
+    Ryzen AI MAX 395 (Radeon 8060S), 128 GiB RAM, ROCm 7.2.4, vLLM `0.32.0+rocm723`,
+    `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `--max-model-len 4096`, otherwise idle machine.
+
+The pool is shared with every host process and container, so only the memory that is free at
+startup can be committed. Size `--gpu-memory-utilization` from `free / total` and leave headroom for
+the host.
+
+Because the denominator is shared with the host, prefer the byte-based `--kv-cache-memory-bytes` over a
+percentage when the footprint has to be reproducible. On the setup above vLLM reports
+`--kv-cache-memory-bytes=113296359936` (105.52 GiB) as the value that fills the pool, i.e. the GTT
+limit minus weights, activations and graph memory.
+
+!!! note "CUDA graph memory profiling"
+    Since v0.21.0 vLLM profiles CUDA graph memory and subtracts it from the requested utilization.
+    On the setup above `--gpu-memory-utilization=0.15` behaves like `0.1467` without profiling, and
+    `0.1533` is needed to obtain the same KV cache size as before. Set
+    `VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=0` to restore the old accounting.
+
+Two device-specific behaviors on `gfx1151`:
+
+- The ROCm custom paged attention kernel is not available, and vLLM logs
+  `Cannot use ROCm custom paged attention kernel, falling back to Triton implementation`.
+  This is expected and needs no flag.
+- Graph capture works. `--enforce-eager` is not required for small models at short context lengths;
+  enable it only when capture fails or stalls.
+
 ## Reduce CUDA Graphs
 
 By default, we optimize model inference using CUDA graphs which take up extra memory in the GPU.

@@ -20,6 +20,12 @@ vLLM supports AMD GPUs with ROCm 6.3 or above. Pre-built wheels are available fo
     - MI350 requires ROCm 7.0 or above
     - Ryzen AI MAX / AI 300 Series requires ROCm 7.0.2 or above
 
+!!! note "Ryzen AI MAX / AI 300 Series"
+    These are unified-memory APUs: there is no dedicated VRAM, and device memory is a window over
+    system RAM shared with the host, which changes how `--gpu-memory-utilization` should be sized.
+    See [Conserving Memory](../../configuration/conserving_memory.md#unified-memory-apus) for
+    measured KV cache sizes and the `gfx1151` notes.
+
 --8<-- [end:requirements]
